The Institute challenged human resource (HR) professionals in Nigeria’s public service to move beyond routine personnel administration and become strategic drivers of institutional transformation.
The charge was delivered at CIPM’s 74th Induction Ceremony, held, Ikeja, Lagos, with the theme, “Beyond Administration: Elevating HR Professionalism for Excellence in Public Service.”
A total of 134 professionals were inducted, comprising eight through the Executive Route and 126 through the Practitioners’ Route.
In his address, the President and Chairman of the Governing Council of CIPM, Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, said professional induction went beyond the acquisition of a designation, stressing that professional credentials must be reflected in the values, integrity and quality of decisions practitioners demonstrate.
“The letters after your name, either ACIPM or MCIPM, must be supported by the values behind your decisions,” Gobir said.
He described CIPM members as ambassadors of the Institute, noting that their conduct, professional decisions and interactions must strengthen its reputation.
He urged the inductees to make meaningful contributions to their organisations and society, emphasising that public office is a trust and that citizens seeking government services are not interruptions to public servants’ work, but the very reason the work exists.
“A government office can be fully staffed and still leave citizens underserved,” he said.
Gobir called on HR professionals to champion employee development, performance, integrity and institutional effectiveness, while questioning outdated practices that hinder public sector productivity.
He said transforming public institutions required fresh thinking and a willingness to improve both people and processes.
Delivering the guest presentation, Mr. Osikoya Adesina Sogo, FCIPM, Council Manager and Head of Administration, Agege Local Government, called for a shift from routine personnel administration to strategic HR professionalism.
He outlined five critical changes required to reposition HR practice in the public service: moving from gatekeeping to enabling performance; replacing reactive staff posting with data-driven workforce planning; shifting from generic training to targeted capability development; moving from reactive discipline to a focus on organisational culture and employee engagement; and going beyond procedural compliance to embrace governance and ethical courage.
Sogo noted that at the local government level, people-management decisions directly affect service delivery, as staff deployment, training, personnel records and industrial harmony influence the quality of services citizens receive.
He stressed that high professional standards and human dignity must coexist, urging public institutions to strengthen employee engagement through fairness, recognition, feedback, accountability and constructive problem-solving.
He also underscored the importance of professional independence, ethical courage and respect for due process, particularly in navigating leadership expectations, civil service regulations and labour relations.
The Vice President of CIPM, Mrs. Chidinma Obiejesi, FCIPM, also highlighted the importance of human capital strategy in transforming public service.
She appreciated the Lagos State Government for its continued partnership with the Institute and called for collective efforts to drive the transformation of the state’s public service.
Similarly, the National Treasurer of CIPM, Mr. Adeyemi Ajayi, FCIPM, Chartered FCIPD, urged the inductees to remain active in the Institute and contribute to its growth through mentoring, coaching, continuous learning and participation in branch, chapter and national activities.
The ceremony also highlighted CIPM’s professional development pathways, encouraging HR professionals to pursue formal recognition through its HR Executive Route and HR Practitioners’ Route, which provide opportunities for practitioners at different career stages to strengthen their competence, credibility and professionalism.
CIPM reaffirmed that stronger public institutions depend on competent, ethical and professionally managed people, stressing that professional recognition is an achievement whose true value lies in the positive impact practitioners make in their workplaces and society.
